accepted.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first bank in India?
accepted.x: Bank of Hindustan is regarded as the first bank in India. The Presidency Bank of Bengal was the first bank of the East India Company.
accepted.tq: Use the direct first-in-the-list recall approach.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early banking institutions in India:
1. The Presidency Bank of Bengal was established in 1806.
2. It was the first bank of the East India Company.
3. It was later renamed the Bank of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Presidency Bank of Bengal was established in 1806, was the first bank of the East India Company and was later known as the Bank of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the institution’s date, status and subsequent name.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: The first Presidency bank in India was established as the:
accepted.x: The first Presidency bank was the Bank of Calcutta, established in 1806. It was subsequently renamed the Bank of Bengal; the Bank of Bombay and Bank of Madras followed in 1840 and 1843 respectively.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original name from the later renamed institution.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Presidency banks in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Bank of Madras
B. Bank of Calcutta
C. Bank of Bombay
D. Bank of Bengal
accepted.x: The Bank of Calcutta was established in 1806, followed by its renaming as the Bank of Bengal, the Bank of Bombay in 1840 and the Bank of Madras in 1843.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest institution first and then place the dated successors.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Awadh Commercial Bank was established at Faizabad in 1881. Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam, Punjab National Bank at Lahore and Equitas Small Finance Bank has its head office at Chennai.
accepted.tq: Use the location filter to separate similar banking institutions.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Punjab National Bank, established in 1894, is described as the:
o: First bank of the East India Company
First public sector bank in India
First bank established in Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Punjab National Bank was established in 1894 and is described as the second bank established by Indians. The first public sector bank was the State Bank of India in 1955.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the bank’s rank among Indian-founded banks and other historical firsts.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Who founded Andhra Bank, and on which date was it founded?
accepted.x: Andhra Bank was founded by Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya on 20 November 1923 at Machilipatnam.
accepted.tq: Combine the founder and date instead of relying on a single-name clue.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: The head office of Andhra Bank was known as:
accepted.x: The head office of Andhra Bank was known as Pattabhi Bhavan. The bank was founded at Machilipatnam.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official name rather than the city of establishment.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Which of the following institutions was NOT founded by Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
accepted.x: Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Insurance Company, Bharat Lakshmi Bank and the Krishna District Co-operative Bank. Punjab National Bank was established separately in 1894.
accepted.tq: Find the one institution outside the founder’s associated group.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about banking in nineteenth-century Andhra is correct?
o: Several Presidency banks were established in Andhra during the nineteenth century.
The first bank in Andhra was established at Machilipatnam in 1804.
Andhra had a banking network before Madras received its first banks.
There were no banks in nineteenth-century Andhra, although banking later reached towns such as Machilipatnam.
accepted.x: There were no banks in nineteenth-century Andhra. Banking later reached towns such as Machilipatnam; the listed early banks in Madras included Karnataka Bank, Madras Bank and Asiatic Bank.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute historical claims and identify the carefully worded regional statement.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s: Which of the following was the first bank in India to introduce an ATM?
accepted.x: HSBC introduced the first ATM in India in Mumbai in 1987. Central Bank of India is associated with the first credit card in India, not the first ATM.
accepted.tq: Separate the first ATM from other banking firsts such as the first credit card.
accepted.sec: Bank founders, headquarters and firsts (Andhra Bank, PNB, first ATM, first SFB, SBI OBU)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Capital Small Finance Bank — Jalandhar
2. Equitas Small Finance Bank — Chennai
3. SBI’s first overseas banking unit — Mumbai
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Capital Small Finance Bank was established at Jalandhar, Equitas Small Finance Bank has its head office at Chennai and SBI’s first overseas banking unit was located in Mumbai.
accepted.tq: Verify each institution-location pair independently before selecting the code.

accepted.s: The first bank with wholly Indian capital and management was:
accepted.x: Punjab National Bank is described as the first bank with wholly Indian capital and management. Awadh Commercial Bank was the first bank run by Indians with limited liability and an all-Indian board.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the broader ownership-and-management distinction from the first Indian-run bank.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first private bank established after the 1994 liberalisation of banking in India?
o: UTI Bank, now known as Axis Bank
accepted.x: UTI Bank was the first private bank established after the 1994 liberalisation of banking. It is now known as Axis Bank.
accepted.tq: Match the historical first with its former and present identity.

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is an example of para-banking?
o: Distributing mutual funds and providing insurance services
accepted.x: Para-banking refers to services beyond the traditional acceptance of deposits and provision of loans, including credit cards, insurance, factoring and mutual fund distribution. Credit to paramilitary personnel is not para-banking merely because of the category of borrower.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition by separating ancillary financial services from ordinary banking or lending.

accepted.s: The penalty scheme for an ATM remaining out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month came into effect from:
accepted.x: From 1 October 2021, a penalty of ₹10,000 per ATM applies when an ATM remains out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month. The June 2019 RBI order preceded the implementation of this penalty scheme.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of the regulatory order from the date on which the penalty scheme took effect.
accepted.sec: Banking operations and customer rules - para-banking, cheque validity, ATM penalty, assets vs liabilities

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a liability of a commercial bank?
accepted.x: Customer deposits are liabilities because the bank owes these amounts to depositors. Loans, investments and cash reserves are assets of the bank.
accepted.tq: Apply the ownership-and-obligation test to distinguish assets from liabilities.
accepted.sec: Banking operations and customer rules - para-banking, cheque validity, ATM penalty, assets vs liabilities

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an asset of a commercial bank?
o: Balances maintained with the Reserve Bank of India
accepted.x: Borrowings are liabilities of a commercial bank. Cash in hand, balances with the RBI, investments, loans and advances, and fixed assets are bank assets.
accepted.tq: Find the item representing an obligation rather than a resource owned or controlled by the bank.
accepted.sec: Banking operations and customer rules - para-banking, cheque validity, ATM penalty, assets vs liabilities

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding collateral-free credit is correct?
o: Only loans to large industries up to ₹25 lakh are collateral-free.
MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh and all PMEGP units must be collateral-free, with banks permitted to raise the limit to ₹25 lakh.
Collateral-free lending is available only to agricultural borrowers.
All MSE loans above ₹20 lakh must compulsorily be secured by collateral.
accepted.x: MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh and all PMEGP units must be provided without collateral. Banks may raise the collateral-free limit to ₹25 lakh under the applicable RBI directions.
accepted.tq: Read the threshold and the exception together instead of treating the limit as universal.
